title: Implemented controller scope and data flow
academic_purpose: 区分原创编排、upstream replay与策略作用范围
demonstrates: Figure 3.4 locates the learnt controller within the implemented HRC system. The policy replaces replay only inside ExecuteBehaviorTask, while the surrounding interaction and transition logic remains scripted. Source identity is retained from recording through export to the diagnostic benchmark.
caption: Implemented controller scope and data flow. (a) The recorded finite-state schedule; non-final rounds continue through WaitNextCommand and Relocate, while the final round exits from FaceHuman to AllTasksDone. (b) ExecuteBehaviorTask uses upstream state/action replay for dataset construction and the predicted-action client for policy rollout. (c) Source-level quality control and splitting precede diagnostic use of the exported data. High-level phases are supplied by the scripted scheduler.

source: rescan_qc.json; 45 HDF5 sources; final export manifests/reports; parquet alignment audit

caption: Training diagnostics for the three 20,000-update runs (one training seed, 42, per configuration). The training objective was logged every 100 updates and the monitored validation objective every 1,000 updates. All 32 model output dimensions, including padding, contribute to the normalised flow objective. Different supervision and normalisation pipelines prevent interpreting these magnitudes as directly comparable physical-action errors or task-success measures.
